belief.statement: The guideline ranks ribociclib above abemaciclib and palbociclib, so it is the better drug.
belief.how_we_know_they_believe_it: The category difference is reported without the preference designation. We held this belief ourselves and published it.

carried_by.what_it_said: reported the categories without the preference system

carried_by.outlet: What Holds Up, issue two, first version

what_the_sources_show.statement: NCCN v6.2026 lists all three combinations as Preferred. Only the category of evidence differs, and the guideline makes no comparative efficacy claim.
sources: NCCN v6.2026, read by the operator

reader_with_a_decision: A patient choosing between three drugs, or a clinician explaining to a patient why one carries a different label.

prior_art_found: OncLive and Pharmacy Times carried the preference distinction
public_record_check.carried_in_general_coverage: Partly. Two clinical outlets carried it; the general reporting did not, and neither did we.
public_record_check.our_contribution: translation, and a correction of ourselves

sources_are_open: NO — NCCN's licence forbids any automated check reading it. This is why the error survived.
evidence_base_is_bounded: the guideline yes; the comparative literature no, which is where the false universals came from
lead_came_from: a Signal inquiry, which is a lead and not a premise
_backfilled: Recorded retroactively on 2026-08-29 when the entry gate was rebuilt around the belief test. Kept so the contrarianism guard has something to count.

kill_condition_tested._note: Filled in AFTER going to look, by whoever looked. This one was not tested before publication. It was met, by an outside reader, the day after.
kill_condition_tested.note: The condition was MET: all three AI+CDK4/6 combinations are listed as preferred and only the category of evidence differs. Recorded as 'narrowed' rather than 'killed' because the piece survives in a smaller and better form -- it is now about an evidence label being read as a ranking, which is a claim the piece can evidence from its own conduct. Had this been tested before drafting, the piece would have been written that way from the start and the correction would not have been needed.

kill_condition: If the guideline itself distinguishes the strength of its evidence from its preference between the regimens -- for instance by listing all three combinations as equally preferred -- then the guideline is not ranking the drugs, the premise as drafted is false, and the piece has to be about how the label is READ rather than about what the guideline claims.
